note: DEMO CONTENT, DERIVED by research-agent on 2026-11-12, revised the same day after research review 001 (F-14: the arithmetic now follows from the basis, and the RISK-003 widening is applied). No frozen delivery baseline exists (.mw/metrics/ is empty) and no delivery history exists (GAP-006 waived), so both ranges are judgement from the size measures below, not calibrated. Person-days count human effort (review, decisions, gates, pairing); agent compute time is not counted. This file belongs to the RESEARCH_ESTIMATE branch, which is still open; research-agent owns it.
basis: Size, STATED in research/inputs/baseline-metrics.md: 2,123 Python source lines, 6 capabilities, 81 business rules (80 live after the retirement of L1-posting/BR-009), 54 test functions; and from the code at e1fbd3a: 40 HTTP endpoints, 5 enum types, 1 SQLite database

Behaviour is already specified: the confirmed baseline has a rules-trace per capability, and all 7 conflicts and 21 open questions were settled by a human at the baseline gate, so discovery effort is not in either range
Existing test coverage, DERIVED (RISK-004): about 50 of 81 rule sections cite a Python test, so about 31 parity tests are written from the rules-trace alone

Traditional (DERIVED), step by step: Rust code 3,000 to 5,000 lines (for about 2,000 lines of Python) at 100 to 150 reviewed lines a day = 20 to 50 days; parity harness 5 to 8 days; data-compatibility work 4 to 8 days; about 31 new parity tests at 0.1 to 0.25 days each = 3 to 8 days. Subtotal 32 to 74 days. Plus the RISK-003 widening of 2 to 5 days = 34 to 79 person-days

Agentic (DERIVED), step by step: agents draft the specs, parity tests and Rust code per capability from the rules-trace; human effort goes to the gates (research, PRD, plan, PR reviews), the Rust platform ADR (DEP-003), the data-compatibility review (ASM-002) and fixing parity failures that need judgement. 6 capability stories at 2 to 4 human days = 12 to 24; the platform story (app wiring, errors, config, data layer) 1 to 2; the parity-harness story 1 to 2; fixed overhead 0 to 1. Subtotal 14 to 29 days. Plus the RISK-003 widening of 2 to 5 days = 16 to 34 person-days

Six capabilities can be built in waves along the baseline's dependency order (Accounts first, then Following, then Posting, Timelines, Notifications, Moderation), which bounds the high end for both approaches
change-sizing (DERIVED): this is not a same-day change; at major classification it should be split into at least one story per capability plus a platform story and a parity-harness story

widening.GAP-006: No delivery history and no frozen .mw/metrics/baseline.json: no calibration, so both ranges are wide (high is about 2x low)
widening.GAP-004: No incident history: unknown edge cases in existing data could add data-compatibility work (DEP-005); not added to the numbers, it pushes toward the high end
widening.RISK-003: Framework-level behaviour (validation error bodies, JSON formats, docs routes) is not specified; deciding and matching it adds 2 to 5 days, APPLIED to both ranges above
widening.RISK-010: Text-processing parity (regex dialect, code-point lengths, Unicode case folding) is inside the per-capability and harness days; a regex engine without lookbehind would push toward the high end
widening.DEP-003: Rust stack not chosen yet; an unfamiliar framework or driver would push both ranges toward the high end
